issues.description:
Method: messageOnMilk
Problem statement: In the UML and interface section the milk method is declared as messageOnMilk() with no parameters (returns String). However, in Part 2 the instructions describe a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume). Template and solution: the provided Main (template) and the solution interface/class implementations define and call messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This conflicting specification (no-arg vs. double parameter) creates uncertainty about the correct method signature and will cause compilation/signature mismatches if a student implements the parameterized version or follows the no-arg version depending on which part they follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the specification of messageOnMilk across all artifacts. Prefer the minimal-change option: update the Part 2 textual instruction to require a no-argument method messageOnMilk() that returns the string "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (matching the UML, template Main usage, and the provided solution). Alternatively (larger change), update the UML, template Main, and solution to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) consistently and adjust examples/tests accordingly. Recommend option A (no-arg) to preserve existing template and solution code.

issues.description: Conflicting signatures for the same conceptual operation "milking an animal": the problem text describes a method named messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (problem_statement.md line 93) while the UML and all code artifacts use a parameterless messageOnMilk(). Specifically: the UML declares messageOnMilk() with no parameters (problem_statement.md line 52); the template Main calls m.messageOnMilk() with no argument (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 31); and the solution defines the interface method as String messageOnMilk() (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5). Students cannot reliably map the problem requirement to the provided template code because implementing one signature will not satisfy the other, causing compilation errors or incorrect behavior.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the messageOnMilk contract consistent across all artifacts. Either:
(A) Conform the problem statement to the code: update the textual description (and UML if desired) to require a parameterless messageOnMilk() that returns a simple message (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked") to match the template and solution; OR
(B) Update the code artifacts to accept a double parameter: change the Milkable interface to String messageOnMilk(double milkVolume), update all implementations (Seal, Goat, etc.) to implement the signature and include the volume in their return string, and update template Main and any tests to call messageOnMilk(...) with an appropriate milkVolume. Option (A) is the minimal change to align with the provided template and solution; option (B) is viable if the intention is to record volumes, but requires updating interface, implementations, template usage, and tests.
